checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer send proof_bytes with incorrect length to cause crash or memory corruption?
checklist_item.bug_class: Buffer Overflow via Malformed Proof Length

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: KzgProofs and KzgCommitments are stored as [][]byte with ssz-size tag enforcing exactly 48 bytes per element. The Column field enforces 2048 bytes per element. Any deviation causes ssz.DivideInt2 to fail with an error during UnmarshalSSZ, preventing the malformed message from entering the Go layer.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The SSZ UnmarshalSSZ uses DivideInt2 for commitments and proofs — returns error if buffer not evenly divisible by 48. length-1, length+1, or zero cannot produce valid slices. decodePubsubMessage propagates ssz.ErrSize as ValidationReject before any Go-level processing occurs.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Malicious P2P message passes through decodePubsubMessage (SSZ UnmarshalSSZ). For malformed proof/commitment byte lengths the SSZ decoder returns error causing ValidationReject before any KZG operations are reached.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: SSZ enforces fixed 48-byte elements for KzgCommitments/KzgProofs and fixed 2048-byte elements for Column. No incorrect-length proof_bytes can survive deserialization. No crash or memory corruption possible at the Go layer.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — vulnerability precondition does not exist
audit_items.recommendation: No action required. SSZ deserialization enforces fixed element lengths before any KZG code is reached.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch validate that commitment_bytes[], cells[], and proof_bytes[] arrays have consistent lengths?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: VerifyDataColumnSidecar (p2p_interface.go:47) explicitly checks len(Column)==len(KzgCommitments)==len(KzgProofs), returning ErrMismatchLength on failure. VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs builds slices by iterating sidecar.Column range with same-index access, guaranteeing consistent lengths before passing to ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch independently checks all four array lengths are equal, returning ErrBadArgs on mismatch. Consistency check exists at three independent layers: SSZ, Go application, and C library.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: VerifyDataColumnSidecar is called as RequireValidFields before KZG verification. Any mismatch returns ErrMismatchLength causing ValidationReject.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: SG-021:INV-001 holds: array length consistency enforced at three independent layers. Index-out-of-bounds during batch iteration is impossible.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — three independent enforcement layers guarantee array length consistency

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does the P2P gossip validation layer enforce byte length constraints before data reaches verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: P2P deserialization path enforces SSZ fixed-size fields: Column 2048 bytes, KzgCommitments/KzgProofs 48 bytes each. SSZ DivideInt2 rejects any non-divisible buffer. After SSZ, ValidFields calls VerifyDataColumnSidecar which enforces array count consistency.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No bypass path exists: decodePubsubMessage applies SSZ before any application logic sees the data. Wrong commitment/proof byte lengths cannot reach validateDataColumn's verifier methods or VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker-controlled P2P bytes pass through: (1) SSZ decoder enforcing field byte lengths, (2) VerifyDataColumnSidecar enforcing array count consistency, (3) ckzg4844 binding enforcing slice lengths. No bypass of any of these three layers exists.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Defense-in-depth fully implemented: byte length at SSZ layer, count consistency at application layer, array equality at C library layer. The property that validateDataColumn independently validates before reaching KZG is proven.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — P2P validation layer fully enforces all byte length constraints
audit_items.recommendation: No action required. Defense-in-depth is intact.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does bytes_to_kzg_commitment perform BLS12-381 G1 subgroup check during deserialization?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: In the Go layer, commitments are passed as raw Bytes48 to ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch which delegates to the C library. The C library's verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch calls compute_weighted_sum_of_commitments, which calls bytes_to_kzg_commitment for each unique commitment. bytes_to_kzg_commitment calls validate_kzg_g1 (bytes.c:81), which calls blst_p1_in_g1 to verify prime-order subgroup membership, returning C_KZG_BADARGS on failure.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Any attacker-provided commitment bytes representing a BLS12-381 curve point outside G1 prime-order subgroup will cause blst_p1_in_g1 to return false, propagating as C_KZG_BADARGS error. No path allows a non-subgroup commitment to be accepted.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Both P2P path (validateDataColumn -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch) and Engine API path (VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch) call ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch containing the C-level subgroup check.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: bytes_to_kzg_commitment returns C_KZG_BADARGS iff point is not on BLS12-381 curve or not in G1 prime-order subgroup. blst_p1_in_g1 in validate_kzg_g1 (c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:92) is the correct enforcement.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — subgroup check correctly enforced at C library layer
audit_items.recommendation: No fix required. The Go code relies on the C library for subgroup enforcement, which is correctly implemented in c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does bytes_to_kzg_proof perform BLS12-381 G1 subgroup check during deserialization?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Proof bytes are passed as Bytes48 slices through kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> C verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. Inside the C library, bytes_to_kzg_proof is called for each proof, which calls validate_kzg_g1, enforcing both curve-membership and prime-order subgroup checks before any pairing operations.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A P2P attacker providing a DataColumnSidecar with a non-subgroup KZG proof point will have it rejected by bytes_to_kzg_proof (via blst_p1_in_g1) before any pairing computation. No execution path allows a non-subgroup proof to reach the pairings_verify call.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Both P2P and Engine API paths call C-level verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch, where bytes_to_kzg_proof enforces subgroup membership on every proof point before cryptographic aggregation.
entry_points: beacon-chain/sync: validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg (P2P gossip, attacker-controlled proof bytes)

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: bytes_to_kzg_proof rejects all non-subgroup points via blst_p1_in_g1. The proof path in c-kzg-4844 eip7594.c is identical to the commitment path. No bypass in v2.1.1.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — subgroup check correctly enforced at C library layer for proof points
audit_items.recommendation: No fix required. Subgroup validation for proof points correctly implemented at C library level.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: What is the impact on the pairing check if non-subgroup points are accepted?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Both bytes_to_kzg_commitment and bytes_to_kzg_proof in c-kzg-4844 call validate_kzg_g1 (bytes.c:81-95), which calls blst_p1_in_g1 to verify G1 prime-order subgroup membership. Any non-subgroup point returns C_KZG_BADARGS propagating as error through the Go binding.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For a non-subgroup G1 point: blst_p1_uncompress succeeds (on curve), blst_p1_in_g1 returns false, validate_kzg_g1 returns C_KZG_BADARGS. The sidecar is rejected. Non-subgroup points cause an error path, not a false-positive verification.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Non-subgroup bytes are caught inside compute_weighted_sum_of_commitments (bytes_to_kzg_commitment) and bytes_to_kzg_proof, both calling validate_kzg_g1 with blst_p1_in_g1. The pairing check security assumption is upheld.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The pairing check security assumption (all points in correct subgroup) is enforced by validate_kzg_g1 for both commitments and proofs before the pairing equation is evaluated.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — non-subgroup points rejected before any pairing operations

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can malicious P2P peer bypass subgroup checks via crafted DataColumnSidecar?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Complete P2P path: decodePubsubMessage (SSZ) -> ValidFields (VerifyDataColumnSidecar) -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (Go) -> verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (C) -> validate_kzg_g1 -> blst_p1_in_g1. Subgroup validation enforced at C library layer.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A DataColumnSidecar with valid BLS12-381 curve point but wrong subgroup: passes SSZ (checks byte length only), passes VerifyDataColumnSidecar (checks array lengths only), but fails at validate_kzg_g1 via blst_p1_in_g1. Returns C_KZG_BADARGS causing ValidationReject. No bypass path exists.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Non-subgroup points can reach the KZG library call but are caught there. The subgroup check is correctly placed at the cryptographic library layer and enforced for every commitment and proof.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Subgroup check correctly implemented in cryptographic library layer (blst_p1_in_g1). No bypass exists. Single-layer validation at the crypto library is standard and sufficient practice.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: c-kzg-4844 bytes.c:92 blst_p1_in_g1 called from validate_kzg_g1 for every commitment and proof

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — subgroup validation correctly enforced in C cryptographic library
audit_items.recommendation: No action required. Single-layer subgroup validation in the crypto library is consistent with industry practice for BLS12-381.

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Does verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch assume inputs have passed subgroup validation?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The Go binding VerifyCellKZGProofBatch calls ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch, which calls C-level verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. This function calls bytes_to_kzg_commitment (via compute_weighted_sum_of_commitments) and bytes_to_kzg_proof, both calling validate_kzg_g1 -> blst_p1_in_g1. Subgroup validation is internal to the function.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch performs its own internal subgroup validation, not relying on callers. Call sites pass raw bytes without pre-validation, but the C library validates internally before any cryptographic operations.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No call site pre-validates subgroup membership; all validation happens inside the function. The function owns its security invariants — correct design pattern.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch does not assume pre-validated inputs; it performs subgroup validation internally via validate_kzg_g1. No implicit trust assumption exists.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — function performs its own subgroup validation internally

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Which cryptographic library implements the BLS12-381 subgroup check, and is it correct?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm uses github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/v2 v2.1.1 for cell KZG operations. This uses blst (Supranational's BLST library) for BLS12-381 operations. Subgroup check is blst_p1_in_g1, which verifies G1 prime-order subgroup membership via scalar multiplication by the group order.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: c-kzg-4844 is the Ethereum Foundation's official KZG implementation, audited by multiple security firms. blst is widely deployed in production ETH2 clients. No known CVEs affect subgroup checks in v2.1.1.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The subgroup check implementation (blst_p1_in_g1) is in the blst C library. c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1 calls it correctly in validate_kzg_g1 for both commitments and proofs.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1 with blst correctly implements BLS12-381 G1 subgroup checks. validate_kzg_g1 is the standard pattern used across all EIP-4844 implementations. No mathematical incorrectness identified.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — well-audited, production-grade library with correct subgroup check
audit_items.recommendation: No action required. Monitor upstream c-kzg-4844 releases for security advisories.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does commitment deduplication in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch preserve semantic equivalence?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: deduplicate_commitments (eip7594.c:343-374) implements quadratic deduplication: for each commitment i, scans existing unique commitments for byte-equal match. If found, indices_out[i]=j (existing). If not, appended at new_count and indices_out[i]=new_count. Straightforward, correct bijective mapping.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Invariant deduplicated_commitments[commitment_indices[k]] == original_commitments_bytes[k] holds by construction. No off-by-one exists. Weight aggregation uses commitment_indices[i] < num_commitments, preventing out-of-bounds.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The weight aggregation uses commitment_indices[i] as index into commitment_weights[]. Since commitment_indices[i] < num_commitments by construction, no out-of-bounds access is possible. Semantic equivalence preserved.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: SG-021:INV-003 holds: deduplication algorithm correct by construction with proper index assignment for both existing and new entries.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — deduplication algorithm is correct by construction

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Is the commitment_indices mapping bijective on equivalence classes?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The deduplicate_commitments function maps each cell's commitment to a unique index via byte-equality scan. Surjective: every index in [0, num_commitments) referenced by at least one cell. The mapping from equivalence classes to unique indices is a proper quotient map.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For byte-wise identical commitments, all cells sharing that commitment have the same commitment_indices value. Weight accumulation correctly sums all r^k for k corresponding to cells with same commitment. Bijective property on equivalence classes holds.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Algorithm is deterministic and pure. Identical commitments always map to same unique index regardless of input order. No information loss in equivalence class mapping.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Bijective on equivalence classes: each equivalence class maps to exactly one unique commitment index, and each unique commitment index has at least one cell. Proven by inspection of eip7594.c:343-374.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: eip7594.c:354-373 deduplication loop with commitments_equal byte comparison

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — bijective mapping correctly maintained

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer exploit commitment deduplication to forge valid proofs?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: P2P peer can control which commitments appear in DataColumnSidecar and their ordering. However, deduplication uses byte-equality so index assignment is deterministic on commitment byte content. Attacker cannot cause index confusion — mapping determined solely by commitment bytes.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Attack: two distinct cells claiming same commitment. Result: deduplication correctly identifies them as equal, gives same commitment_indices value. Weight equals sum of their r^k values — correct behavior. No index confusion achievable. Proof forgery requires solving discrete log.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker controlling commitment ordering cannot cause commitment_indices to map a cell to the wrong commitment because the mapping is purely content-addressed (byte equality). Forging valid proof via deduplication confusion requires breaking KZG commitment binding.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Commitment deduplication off-by-one attack vector not viable: algorithm is provably correct and content-addressed. Proof forgery via deduplication requires breaking KZG binding (computationally infeasible).
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Content-addressed deduplication (byte equality) in eip7594.c commitments_equal

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — no exploitable commitment deduplication confusion path exists

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: What is the impact on validator-node if commitment deduplication fails?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: If deduplication failed and invalid proof accepted: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs returns nil -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier returns ValidationAccept -> sidecar stored as VerifiedRODataColumn -> downstream consumers treat as valid data availability proof. However, as proven in CHK-0125/0126/0127, this scenario is not achievable.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Commitment deduplication is correct and cannot be exploited. Hypothetical scenario of accepted invalid proof due to deduplication failure has no achievable counterexample. Impact analysis is theoretical only.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Theoretical impact: incorrect data availability attestations by validator nodes could affect consensus safety. However, this path requires the deduplication algorithm to be broken, which it is not.
entry_points: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs (hypothetical failure) -> validateDataColumn accepts sidecar -> DAS processing

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Impact question is moot because deduplication algorithm is proven correct. Hypothetical severity would be high (consensus safety) but precondition does not exist in this codebase.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Deduplication correctness proven in CHK-0125/0126/0127; no deduplication bug exists

audit_items.severity_assessment: Theoretical severity high if bug existed; actual risk zero as precondition does not exist
audit_items.recommendation: No action required. Theoretical severity noted for documentation.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs reject input with fewer than 50% cells?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars enforces 50% threshold in two steps: (1) deduplication via map[uint64]blocks.VerifiedRODataColumn keyed by Index ensures only unique columns counted, then (2) uint64(sidecarCount) < MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() performs strict less-than check. For NumberOfColumns=128, threshold=64 (exactly 50%). Zero-input caught by prior len==0 check.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: 63 unique sidecars: 63 < 64 = true -> ErrNotEnoughDataColumnSidecars. 64 unique sidecars: 64 < 64 = false -> proceeds. Duplicate indices collapsed by map. c-kzg-4844 C library also independently validates (defense-in-depth). No counterexample found.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Call site data_columns_reconstruct.go:reconstructDataColumns independently checks storedColumnsCount < MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() before calling, providing a second pre-filter. Defense-in-depth at both caller and callee.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: SG-024:INV-002 holds. Proven by: strict less-than comparison, deduplication guard, unit tests confirming minimum-1 returns ErrNotEnoughDataColumnSidecars while exactly 50% succeeds.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: reconstruction.go uint64(sidecarCount) < MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct(); map deduplication on Index

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — 50% threshold correctly enforced at both Go and C library layers

checklist_item.title: Supporting Check: Is the 50% threshold correctly derived from CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB constant?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Formula (N+1)/2 implements ceiling division: for even N=128, yields N/2=64 (50%); for odd N, yields ceil(50%), correct for rate-2 Reed-Solomon. NumberOfColumns=128 in both config/fieldparams/mainnet.go and config/params/mainnet_config.go, equal to CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB=128.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Off-by-one confirmed correct: threshold 64 accepts exactly 64 columns, rejects 63. sidecarCount is int from len(map), cast to uint64 — no overflow for max realistic value 128. NumberOfColumns is startup constant, not modifiable at runtime by external input.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Formula (N+1)/2 equals ceil(N/2), the mathematically required threshold for rate-2 Reed-Solomon recovery. Configuration constant is immutable during node operation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Proven by: mathematical equivalence of (N+1)/2 to ceil(N/2), unit tests confirming N=128->64, N=129->65, N=130->65, and immutability of config constant during operation.

audit_items.severity_assessment: Not applicable — threshold correctly implements ceil(50%) via (N+1)/2 formula
audit_items.recommendation: No action required. Threshold calculation is mathematically correct and resistant to off-by-one errors.
